Potassium Citrate + Citric Acid: Recommended in AUA and EAU guidelines for hypocitraturic calcium oxalate stones, uric acid and cystine stones. First approval/introduction: Long-established pharmacopoeial alkaliniser (IP/BP/USP). Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6): Vitamin B6; included in some urinary alkaliniser solutions to reduce oxalate generation. First approval/introduction: Isolated 1938; pharmacopoeial vitamin.

stated in product list – common marketed strength)
Citrate alkalinises urine and inhibits crystal formation; pyridoxine helps reduce endogenous oxalate production.

Potassium Citrate + Citric Acid Citrate is metabolised to bicarbonate, raising urinary pH and urinary citrate. Alkaline urine increases solubility of uric acid and cystine; citrate binds calcium and inhibits calcium oxalate/phosphate crystal formation. Relieves dysuria of lower urinary tract infection. Receptor / target profile: Systemic alkalinisation raises urinary pH and citrate, which complexes calcium and inhibits crystal nucleation and growth.

Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) Cofactor in amino-acid metabolism; reduces endogenous oxalate production (glyoxylate shunting), useful in oxalate stone formers. Receptor / target profile: Coenzyme (as pyridoxal 5'-phosphate) for transamination; diverts glyoxylate away from oxalate formation.
